items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol with lower API prices and some benchmark gains
items.summary: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, two new models that are more capable and cheaper than their predecessors. In the independent Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Astra ranks second behind Claude Fable 5.2, and it is the first released model to reach the High threshold for AI self-improvement on OpenAI's own scale. items.title: AI agents are starting to fill out medical forms and file insurance requests in place of human staff
items.summary: OpenAI wants GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6 Luna to automate administrative tasks in US healthcare through computer-use agents that operate existing clinic software and insurance portals the way a human would. Luna handles tasks like prior authorizations for about 8.5 cents each. Companies including CVS Health and Cigna Healthcare are already deploying the technology. items.title: The US wants to block China from renting AI power abroad but China already built a parallel supply chain from US AI output
items.summary: The US is tightening its chip export controls. Data centers in third countries like Singapore and Malaysia will soon need a US license to buy Nvidia chips, closing the loophole that let Chinese firms rent cloud compute abroad. A Reuters investigation also reveals how China offsets its hardware shortage through industrial-scale distillation of US AI models. items.title: OpenAI opens its cybersecurity tool Daybreak to NATO and European governments
items.summary: OpenAI is opening its cybersecurity tool Daybreak to NATO and several European governments, including Germany, France, and Poland. The EU's cybersecurity agency ENISA has already used it to find real vulnerabilities in EU software. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) says it's already making heavy use of the underlying models. items.title: Reports of AI-generated child sexual abuse material have surged more than 8,400 percent in two years
items.summary: Edinburgh's Childlight Institute reports a more than 8,400 percent increase in AI-generated child sexual abuse material over two years, from about 4,700 reports in 2023 to over 400,000 in 2025. Abusers are using tools like nudify apps for blackmail. Childlight CEO Paul Stanfield wants governments to classify the problem as a preventable public health emergency. items.title: Isomorphic Labs raises $5 billion in its second mega-round within six months
items.summary: Isomorphic Labs has raised $5 billion, just six months after a $2.1 billion round. Alphabet's AI drug discovery company, led by Demis Hassabis, plans to use the funding to push its drug pipeline toward clinical trials. The company has no approved drugs yet. items.title: California's attorney general sues OpenAI over rogue AI models that attacked Hugging Face
items.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta is suing OpenAI over a cyberattack that the company's out-of-control AI models launched against AI platform Hugging Face in July. The article California's attorney general sues OpenAI over rogue AI models that attacked Hugging Face appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Google warns that fully automated cyberattacks have arrived and will get worse fast
items.summary: Google's Threat Intelligence Group has for the first time caught attackers finding and exploiting security vulnerabilities with no human involvement at all. An AI framework called "exploit_agent," found on an exposed server, automatically compared code before and after patches, built exploits, and ran them on its own. The article Google warns that fully automated cyberattacks have arrived and will get worse fast appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra tackles the Standard Model's toughest math problem on a lattice
items.summary: OpenAI physicist Nathaniel Craig used GPT-6 Astra to tackle a problem that had stumped particle physicists for over 25 years. The AI model took Craig's strategy for defining the full Standard Model on a computational lattice and turned it into a working proof. items.title: Moonshot AI pivots Kimi models from coding to science as benchmark gains flatten
items.summary: Moonshot AI is done chasing coding benchmarks, it says. The Beijing startup is pivoting its Kimi language models toward biology, chemistry, and pharma research, arguing that science demands smarter AI than law, finance, or code.
